semantic: The Anticipated Actual Take-Off Time (AATOT) of the flight.
The designator of an aerodrome. In cases where the  aerodrome forms part of the route description additional  routing information may be provided.
Actual date of arrival.
Actual aerodrome of arrival.
Name of actual aerodrome of arrival if no ICAO location  indicator exists.
Actual date of departure.
List of addressees.
ICAO location indicator of the aerodrome of departure or the  indication ‘AFIL’ meaning an air-filed flight plan or ‘ZZZZ’  when no ICAO location indicator is assigned to the  aerodrome of departure.

Aerodrome of departure used as database key in a query,  may be wild-carded.  May contain an ICAO location indicator or the indication  ‘AFIL’ meaning an air-filed flight plan or ‘ZZZZ’ when no  ICAO location indicator is assigned to the aerodrome of  departure or a combination of alphabetic and wildcard  characters.

The "previous" aerodrome of departure. May contain the  ICAO location indicator or the indication ‘AFIL’ meaning an  air-filed flight plan or ‘ZZZZ’ when no ICAO location indicator  is assigned to the aerodrome of departure.
The ICAO location indicator of the aerodrome of destination  or ‘ZZZZ’ when no ICAO location indicator is assigned to the  aerodrome of destination.

The aerodrome of destination used as database key in a  query, may be wild-carded.  May contain an ICAO location indicator or ‘ZZZZ’ when no  ICAO location indicator has been assigned to the aerodrome  of destination or a combination of alphabetic and wildcard  characters.
The "previous" aerodrome of destination. May contain the  ICAO location indicator or ‘ZZZZ’ when no ICAO location  indicator has been assigned to the aerodrome of destination.
Contains an ADEXP message.
Type of logon parameters ATN or FANS/1A.

Estimate data for an air-filed flight plan.  A point identification, the joining flight level and the estimate  date-time at the point.   NOTE: The flight level indicated is the level at which the  flight has been cleared to join controlled airspace over the  point indicated. It need not be the same as the RFL.
List of ATFCM regulations that affect a flight.

The heading assigned to a flight, expressed in degrees  Must be a three digit numeric or the value ‘ZZZ’ indicating  that no heading is assigned. Optionally, this field may  contain the value ‘PH’ indicating holding the present heading  or the value ‘AW’ indicating that the aircraft is cleared to  avoid weather, but no heading is assigned.
The temperature of the air.

Name of destination alternate aerodrome if no ICAO location  indicator exists. Optionally, the location of the aerodrome if it  is not listed in the national AIP given by bearing and  distance or Lat. Long. Alternatively, if the aircraft did not  depart from an aerodrome, the first point of the route given  by Waypoint/Nav Aid or Lat. Long.
The ICAO location indicator of the first destination alternate  aerodrome or the indicator ‘ZZZZ’ when no ICAO location  indicator has been assigned to the aerodrome.
The ICAO location indicator of the second destination  alternate aerodrome or the indicator ‘ZZZZ’ when no ICAO  location indicator has been assigned to the aerodrome.
The time at which a flight should be overhead the  appropriate Coordination Point (COP) as calculated by the  arrival manager.
The ICAO three-letter designator of the aircraft operator as  indicated in the aircraft identification, ARCID or ICAO Field  7a.
Actual Off_Block Date.
Actual Off_Block Time.
The ICAO three-letter designator of the aircraft operator as  derived from the OPR/ element of ICAO Field 18.
An identifier for a point at which an ATC constraint applies,  either a coded designator of a point or a name given  artificially (GEOxx, RENxx or REFxx).
The approved take off time is the time at which the flight  should take off at the aerodrome as approved by the next  ATC unit.
Approach type of the flight, free text field between 2 and 7  characters.
The ICAO 24-bit aircraft address as used for Mode S,  Datalink. The 'NIL' indication is used to suppress a  previously provided aircraft address.
Aircraft Identification.  May be the registration marking of the aircraft, or the ICAO  designator of the aircraft operator followed by the flight  identifier.
Aircraft Identification used as database key in a query; may  be wild-carded.  Must be a combination of alphanumeric and wild-card  characters up to maximum 7 characters in total.
The "previous" aircraft id. Where the aircraft id. Is to be  amended, the new value will be given in "ARCID".
Type of aircraft (ICAO identification of the type) or ZZZZ.
The status of an airspace expressed as free text indicating if  the area is active or inactive and the type of activity.

An indication of the procedure an arriving aircraft is expected  to fly from the last en-route point.  May be:  - the identifier of a Standard Arrival Route procedure;  - an indication that the aircraft will fly direct to the initial  approach fix;  - an indication that no procedure is specified for the aircraft  to reach the defined point.
An arrival sequence number.

The currently assigned speed of the flight, in kilometres per  hour, knots or Mach number.  Must be 'M' followed by three digits, 'K' or 'N' followed by  four digits or 'ZZZ' indicating that a previously assigned  speed no longer applies.
List of airspaces crossed by a flight.
Actual time of arrival.
Actual time of departure.
The ATFM delay allocated to a flight.
Logon parameters for ATN aircraft.
Logon parameters for ATNB2 equipped aircraft.

ATS route designator and identifiers of first and last points.

Addresses to which ATFM messages should be addressed.
Calculated Date of Arrival
Departure planning status information
Calculated Time of Arrival
Radio communication, navigation and approach equipment  and capabilities (as ICAO field 10a).
Cleared Flight Level. The level currently assigned by ATC to  the flight. It may optionally include a point and a level  restriction at the point.
Indication of a change in either the "flight rules"(VFR/IFR) or  the "type of flight"(OAT/GAT) or both together with the point  at which the change occurs.
Calculated Off-Block Date.
Calculated Off-Block Time.
As ICAO Field 18 COM/. It indicates communications  applications or capabilities.
A general comment in free text without hyphen.
Identification of an ‘exceptional condition’ raised in the  context of ATFM.
The transfer conditions of a flight. A point id or gate id, the  flight level and estimated time at that point and optional  supplementary flight level information.
A co-ordination point identifier, either a coded designator of  a point or a name given artificially (GEOxx, RENxx or  REFxx).

Indication of a cruiseclimb. Giving the point at which the  climb will begin, speed or mach no. and the two levels  indicating the flight level band to be occupied during the  climb. The second level may be "PLUS" where the upper  level is unknown.
An indicator confirming the new co-ordination status of a  flight and the reason for the change.
Calculated Take-Off Date.
Calculated Take-Off Time (CTOT): reference time of an  ATFM Slot.
Indication of the data applications and capabilities carried by  the aircraft.
Days of operation for a repetitive flight plan (1234567 where  1 is for Monday, 2 for Tuesday, ..., with 0 in columns of non- operation).
Days of operation for a repetitive flight plan, used as  database key in a query message, may be wildcarded.
The "previous" days of operation. Used as a database key.  Where the days of operation of an RPL are to be amended,  the new values will be given in "DAYS".
Indicates a direct route between two points.  The points may either be a valid ICAO designator of a point  or a point appearing in a GEO, REN or REF field of the form  GEOxx, RENxx or REFxx.
A period of time representing a delay. The nature of the  delay i.e. delay to a flight, processing delay, etc. is  dependent upon its context.
An indication of the A-CDM capabilities of the aerodrome of  departure
The aircraft type as received from the airport via a DPI  message.

An indication of the procedure a departing aircraft is  expected to fly to reach the first en-route point.  May be:  - the identifier of a Standard Instrument Departure  procedure;  - an indication that the aircraft will fly direct to the first en- route point;  - an indication that no procedure is specified for the aircraft  reach the defined point.
The aircraft registration mark as received from the airport via  a DPI message.
Indicates the status of the flight prior to the departure, e.g.  “DEICING”.

Name of departure aerodrome if no ICAO location indicator  exists. Optionally, the location of the aerodrome if it is not  listed in the national AIP given by bearing and distance or  Lat. Long. Alternatively, if the aircraft did not depart from an  aerodrome, the first point of the route given by  Waypoint/Nav Aid or Lat. Long.
Description of a condition or entity which is of relevance to  the content of the message.

Name of destination aerodrome if no ICAO location indicator  exists. Optionally, the location of the aerodrome if it is not  listed in the national AIP given by bearing and distance or  Lat. Long. Alternatively, if the aircraft did not depart from an  aerodrome, the first point of the route given by  Waypoint/Nav Aid or Lat. Long.
As in ICAO Field 18 DLE/. Used to indicate an en-route  delay or holding.
The status of the DPI Message. It indicates the sub-type of  the DPI message.

FIR identification and the accumulated elapsed time (in  hours and minutes) to the FIR boundary.
Indication of an elapsed time to a position given by latitude  only.
Indication of an elapsed time to a position given by longitude  only.
Point identifier and the accumulated elapsed time to the  point.
Flight Level to be communicated in a coordination in  advance. It shall include the flight level to be applied and  optionally  the point at which this flight level is applied.
The Estimated Landing Time.
The time at which a period of time ends.
The flight plan data which is applicable to a flight at the point  given or at the entry of the flight into the airspace concerned.  One or both of the fields; ‘ptid’, ‘airspdes’, must be present.
Estimated Off-Block Date.
Estimated Off-Block Date used as database key in a query,  may be wildcarded.  Must be a combination of digits and wild-card characters, up  to maximum 6 characters in total.

List of equipment capability codes each followed by a status  value which specifies the current status of the capability.
ADEXP name of erroneous field(s).
Error message text. May optionally contain an error  identification code.

Estimate data. A point id., the estimated flight level (flight  level number) and the estimate date-time at this point  followed optionally by the supplementary flight level (flight  level number followed by the indicator A or B).
Estimated time of arrival.
Estimated Take_Off Date.
Estimated Take-Off Time.
Indicates specific status, capabilities or lack thereof, as  prescribed for use within the EUR region.
Triggering event.
Classification of an event.
Addresses which are provided in addition to those which are  determined automatically i.e. 'extra addresses'. May contain  only the number of addresses or the actual addresses or  both.
Logon parameters from FANS 1/A aircraft.
The route exactly as filed i.e. without any processing.
Day-time group specifying when the message was filed for  transmission.
A flight level band defining the airspace vertically, inclusive  of the flight levels given.
Flight rule, as ICAO field 8.
The ATFM status of a flight.
Type of flight, as ICAO field 8.
Identifier of a ‘Flow Management Position’.
List of FMPs and their associated ATFM regulations.
Radio frequency.
List of flights inside a formation group.

First day of operation for a repetitive flight plan. This is used  to give the actual first day from which flight plans will be  generated from a RPL (see valfrom field) or the first day on  which an amendment to an RPL is effective.

The further routing of a flight. For use within messages  containing estimate data to indicate the further routing of the  flight following the estimate point. It may contain only the  next point or the complete further routing until the  destination.
Point along a route defined by latitude and longitude and  given in the flight plan, as GEOxx (where xx is a sequence  number).
The speed relative to the ground.
An indicator or flag used by IFPS to warn or to notify ATC  units of additional information concerning a flight plan.
List of complete IFPDs matching the database key given in a  query message.  Contains a list of complete information for each individual  flight which matches given query keys.
List of ifpdsum matching the database key given in a query  message.  Contains a list of summarised information for each individual  flight which matches given query keys.
A unique flight plan identifier, assigned by the IFPS.
Provides an indication of the information item(s) within the  flight plan that are inconsistent with the information held  within the system originating the message.
An indication given by IFPS of those fields which have been  modified, and the nature of the modification.
Identifier of the IFPU which is responsible for a query. It  must process the query and answer to it.

Indication of conditions which have been 'ignored' or by- passed in the processing of the message concerned. An  'ignored' condition may be limited to a specific portion of the  route delimited by the route points given. A condition may,  for example, be a time restriction (route access condition),  flight level restriction or TOS violation.

The 'Initial' Off Block Date - the 'off-block date' as given in  the FPL and updated by flight plan associated messages  (DLA, CHG, etc.). This is the reference date used for  accessing the flight plan in the database and is the only 'off- block date' known by the concerned ATS units.  Note: The IOBD is not affected by changes requested or  notified through the exchange of ATFM messages.

The 'Initial' Off Block Time - the 'off-block time' as given in  the FPL and updated by flight plan associated messages  (DLA, CHG, etc.). This is the reference time used for  accessing the flight plan in the database and is the only 'off- block time' known by the concerned ATS units.  Note: The IOBT is not affected by changes requested or  notified through the exchange of ATFM messages.
Contains the initial flight rules, initial flight type and initial  IFPS processing.
List of Active Conditional Routes.

Mach number, in hundredths of a unit and optionally the  point at which the change is requested.
The validity period of a message, inclusive of the times  given.
The identifier of the metering fix.

Alternatively  the designator 'ZZZ' may be used to indicate that a  previously assigned rate of climb/descent no longer applies.  ‘C’ or ‘D’ followed by ‘ZZZ’ can be used to indicate that a  flight is climbing or descending with an unknown rate.

List of time periods and their respective flow rates for an  ATFM condition.
The ready status of a flight.
Information in support of the message dependent on its  context.
Point along a route which is defined in terms of magnetic  bearing and distance from another point and is given the  designator REFxx.
Reference data for message being transmitted.
Registration markings, as ICAO field 18 REG/. In the case of  a formation flight more than one registration may be  provided.
The NM and IATA coded designators indicating the reason  for a regulation.

An indication that the flight is released by the transferring  controller to the receiving controller.  C = released for climb  D = released for descent  T = released for turn  R = released for right turn  L = released for left turn  F = released for all actions

Information concerning the type of activity (training,  photographic mission, etc.) to be performed during a ‘stay’  period in the route of a flight.
As ICAO Field 18 STS/. Reason for special handling.
As ICAO Field 18 SUR/. Used to provide surveillance  applications or capabilities not specified in -SEQPT”.
As ICAO Field 18 TALT/. An indication of the take-off  alternate aerodrome

Identification of a ‘traffic volume’.
Description of a traffic volume.
Time separation in minutes between a coordinated aircraft  and a preceeding aircraft.

Message title.
